rows.rationale: The decision cites KA-C5-001#cl-15 for a check meter requirement, but the application is for HESCOM, while this clause is issued by BESCOM. | The decision ignores KA-C5-006#cl-4 Note ii, which states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a feasibility report.

The proposed capacity is 45.00 kWp, which is below the 50kWp threshold required for a check meter under KA-C5-006#cl-18. | The cumulative solar capacity (95kW) is 95% of the transformer rating (100kVA), exceeding the 80% limit, but the generator failed to cite this as the primary reason.

The cited clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is marked as superseded in the registry lookup. | The rule requires check meters for capacity > 20 kW, but the proposed capacity is exactly 20.00 kWp, making check meters optional.
The generator incorrectly applied the mandatory check meter rule for capacity > 20 kW, whereas the proposed DC capacity is exactly 20.00 kWp.

The decision is premature because the DISCOM portal status shows technical feasibility has not yet been communicated by the licensee. | The generator failed to consider that installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible, which would support an approval despite the lack of a formal report.

The cited clause was superseded by GJ-C3-003, which mandates different accuracy classes for Solar and Net meters. | The generator failed to cite the current applicable regulation (GJ-C3-003) that governs meter accuracy requirements.
The clause DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 is superseded by the 2024 amendment. | Under the new rule, capacity can be up to 5 times the 3000 kW sanctioned load (15000 kW), so 12000 kW is permitted.

The cited regulation UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 on 2019-01-04, making it invalid for an application dated 2023-08-08. | The proposed 1.0 kWp capacity is within the 100% limit of the 2.0 kW sanctioned load and meets the minimum 1 kWp requirement.

The proposed 1.0 kWp capacity meets the 100% demand limit but violates the minimum 1 kWp requirement specified in the proviso of UP-C3-002#cl-5.1. | The generator failed to consider the proviso requiring a minimum capacity of 1 kWp, which is critical for compliance.

The generator cited KA-C5-006#cl-18, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 provides a different threshold of 17.5 kW for check meters which might conflict or supersede depending on the specific system type. | The generator correctly identified the 50kWp threshold for KA-C5-006, but failed to reconcile it with the 17.5kW threshold in KA-C5-001 for SRTPV systems.
The system capacity is 12 kWp, making check meters optional, not mandatory under the cited rule.
The system capacity is 12.00 kWp, which is below the 20 kW threshold where check meters become mandatory.

The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b, which allows two changes per financial year instead of one. | The application complies with the updated rule allowing two changes per year, making the rejection incorrect.
The clause is marked as superseded in the registry lookup. | The generator failed to cite the updated 2024 guidelines which govern capacity limits for GNM/VNM.
The cumulative capacity for BRPL is 50 MW, which is below the 75 MW threshold for the SLD waiver, so rejection is incorrect.
The waiver only applies to 11kV and below networks, but this project uses a 33 kV connection.

The cited clause DL-C3-009 was superseded by DL-C3-015, which provides higher cumulative capacity thresholds for TPDDL. | The generator failed to use the updated DL-C3-015 guidelines which allow for higher cumulative capacity before SLD charges apply. | Under DL-C3-015, TPDDL's threshold is higher than the 50 MW cited, making the rejection based on the 105 MW cumulative capacity incorrect.

The cited 2015 regulation was superseded by the 2019 regulations on 2019-01-04. | The current 2019 regulation allows up to 75% capacity, whereas the transformer is at 78.1% (125/160), making the rejection valid but the cited rule incorrect.

The clause cited was superseded by the 2024 amendment (DL-C3-009#cl-3.8). | The applicable rule allows capacity up to 5 times the sanctioned load (500 kW), making the 600 kWp proposal invalid under the correct threshold.

The clause DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 is marked as superseded in the registry lookup. | The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit (500 kW) specified in the applicable DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 guidelines.
The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit of 500 kW (5 * 100 kW) allowed under the cited rule.

The generator approved the application based on SDO verification, but the DISCOM portal status explicitly states technical feasibility has not been communicated. | The generator failed to consider that installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible, which would support an approval despite the pending communication.

The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2, which expanded VNM applicability to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The proposed 150 kWp capacity is within the 5x sanctioned load limit (20 kW * 5 = 100 kW, but the rule allows up to 10 MW) and does not justify rejection.
The cited clause actually permits Virtual Net Metering for all consumers, which supports the user's request rather than justifying a rejection.

The generator misinterprets the clause; for MSME/Industrial, capacity is allowed irrespective of load under the newer GJ-C3-004#cl-6.2c-ii regulation. | The generator cites this clause but fails to recognize it permits capacity up to sanctioned load for captive consumers, which the 80kW proposal satisfies.

The cited clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is marked as superseded in the registry lookup. | The generator uses a rule for >20kW to justify approval, but the proposed capacity is 18kW, making check meters optional, not mandatory.
The cited rule makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW, but the proposed capacity is 18.00 kWp, making the check meter optional.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal stating 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided', which violates the requirement for systems >17.5 kW.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 mandates a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider the applicable 17.5 kW check meter requirement for this 30 kWp system.

The cumulative capacity (85 kW) is within the 100 kVA transformer limit, but the generator failed to apply the 65% peak capacity limit from GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso. | The 65% cumulative capacity limit (65 kW) is violated by the 85 kW total, making the application ineligible.

The cumulative capacity (70 kW) exceeds the transformer capacity (100 kW) limit if the 65% threshold from GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso applies. | The generator ignored the 65% cumulative capacity limit specified in GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso, which is more restrictive than the cited amendment.

The decision is premature because the DISCOM portal status shows technical feasibility has not yet been communicated by the licensee. | The generator failed to consider the rule stating installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a formal report.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal stating 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided', which violates the requirement for systems >17.5 kW.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider the applicable 17.5 kW threshold for check meter requirements.

This clause was superseded by GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-class. | The generator cited an outdated accuracy requirement of 0.2s instead of the amended 1.0 class for solar generation. | The decision is correct regarding mandatory check meters for >20kW, but the primary rejection reason used an invalid clause.

The proposed meters (1.0 and 0.5S) meet the accuracy requirements specified in the cited clause. | The system capacity is 25 kWp, making a check meter mandatory, but the rejection reason focuses on accuracy instead.

The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing, yet the generator rejected the application despite the consumer meeting all criteria. | The generator failed to consider that the proposed 10kWp capacity exceeds the 8kW sanctioned load, violating the 100% limit rule.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability. | The generator used an outdated, restrictive definition of VNM eligibility instead of the current broad applicability.
The proposed 120 kWp capacity significantly exceeds the consumer's sanctioned load of 30.0 kW, which may violate technical interconnection limits.

The cumulative capacity (55.0 kW) is within the 100 kVA transformer limit, but the generator failed to apply the 65% peak capacity limit from GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso. | The 65% transformer capacity limit must be checked to ensure cumulative solar does not exceed 65 kW (65% of 100 kVA).
The cumulative capacity for BRPL is 95 MW, which exceeds the 75 MW threshold specified in the cited clause for SLD waiver.
The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing up to 999 KW, yet the generator rejected a 6.00 kWp application for a domestic consumer.

The cited regulation UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 on 2019-01-04, making it invalid for a 2023 application. | Under the active UP-C3-002 regulation, the 78kW cumulative capacity is 78% of the 100kVA transformer, which exceeds the 75% limit.

The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b, which allows two changes per financial year instead of one. | While the notice period of one month fails the two-month requirement, the generator cited an outdated rule regarding the frequency of changes.
The cited clause states claims after October 2024 are ineligible, but the regulatory evidence clarifies all Phase II applications are admissible if claims are received by 31.12.2025.

The cited 2024 guidelines are superseded by the 2025 Seventh Amendment guidelines effective from 2026-01-20. | The cumulative capacity for TPDDL under the current 2025 rules is 100 MW, but the portal shows 120 MW, exceeding the waiver threshold.
The cumulative capacity for TPDDL is 120 MW, which exceeds the 100 MW waiver threshold specified in the cited clause.

The cited clause is superseded by the newer GJ-C3-003 regulations. | The generator cited a superseded rule requiring 0.2s accuracy, whereas the applicable regulation allows 0.5S accuracy which the EPC proposal meets.

The generator failed to consider that installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a formal feasibility report. | The decision is premature because the DISCOM portal status shows technical feasibility has not yet been communicated.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The decision fails to account for the capacity limit rule where VNM capacity can be up to 5 times the sanctioned load (30kW * 5 = 150kW), making the 200kWp proposal invalid.

The cited clause confirms VNM applicability, which supports the user's request rather than justifying a rejection. | The proposed 200 kWp capacity is within the 5x sanctioned load limit (30 kW * 5 = 150 kW, wait, 200 > 150), but the cited clause 3.8 is actually 3(8) and the decision logic is contradictory. | The proposed 200 kWp exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit of 150 kW (30 kW * 5), but the generator cited the wrong clause ID for the capacity limit.
